title: Web Service
desc: Reverse proxy, redirect or serve static files by domain, optionally with authentication and WAF
moduleOffTitle: The Web service module is disabled
moduleOffDesc: While the module is disabled, all listening ports are closed. After enabling it, each listener and site takes effect according to its own switch.
empty: No listeners yet. Add one, or import a Lucky config under "Settings → Backup & Migration"
deleteListenerConfirm: Delete this listener and all of its sites?
listenIpPlaceholder: Leave empty to listen on all addresses
tlsHelp: The certificate is chosen automatically from "SSL Certificates" by domain
newListenerHint: A listener only defines the port and HTTPS. After saving, click "Add site" on its card to set domains and backend targets.
defaultSiteHint: The default site handles requests whose domain matches no other site, so it has no domain and cannot be deleted. Keep it disabled if unused.
resetDefaultConfirm: Reset the default site? All its settings will be cleared and it stays disabled.
acceptProxyHelp: Only sources trusted in the global settings are accepted
accessAddrHelp: The site list uses this scheme and port to build clickable, copyable full URLs such as {example}. Leave empty to derive them from the listener; set them when visitors reach it through Protocol Routing, a router port mapping, frp or a CDN with a different scheme or port. Only links are affected, listening and proxying stay the same
typeCloseHelp: Sends nothing and closes the connection (like nginx return 444). Useful for the default site so requests scanning unknown domains get no response; the access log records them as 444.
typeCloseLimit: Closing only withholds the HTTP response: the TCP and TLS handshakes have already completed, so the client can still tell the port is listening; over HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 only the request is reset and the connection stays open; HTTPS requests that get here have already received the certificate. To make scanners see only timeouts afterwards, ban their addresses in Intrusion Prevention.
typeCloseAllow: Close connection drops every request. To let listed IPs in and drop everyone else, set the type to Reverse proxy, choose Allowlist or Blocklist under IP access control on the Security tab (subscribed IP lists can be used), and set When denied to Close connection. This works for the default site too.
targetsPlaceholder: http://192.168.1.10:8080; multiple backends are used round-robin
optSendProxy: Send PROXY v2 to the backend (passes the real IP; the backend must support it)
webAuth: Web auth (the browser shows a sign-in page)
usersPlaceholder: One per line as username:password (the password may be a bcrypt hash)
oauthUsersPlaceholder: One allowed identity per line as provider-key:account, e.g. github:octocat, google:me{'@'}gmail.com, qq:openid. Add a comment after # at the end of a line; github:* matches any GitHub account
providerHelp: Providers must be configured in "Global settings" first
ipSetsEmpty: No subscribed lists yet; add them in global settings
ipSetsHelp: Checked together with the ranges above; matching any of them counts as being on the list
denyActionHelp: How requests rejected by a ban, IP access control (including path rules) or the country filter are handled. Close connection sends nothing and drops the request, logged as 444, so you can let your own IPs in and drop everyone else.
ipSetsWhitelistHelp: Checked together with the ranges above; matching any of them grants access. Until a list downloads it counts as empty, so the allowlist denies access
requestHeadersPlaceholder: Sent to the backend, one Key: Value per line; an empty Value removes the header
responseHeadersPlaceholder: Returned to the client, one Key: Value per line; an empty Value removes the header
trustedPlaceholder: One IP or subnet per line; leave empty to trust no source
realIPDivider: Visitor real IP (behind a CDN / WAF)
realIPFromPlaceholder: One IP or subnet per line, such as your CDN's origin-pull ranges; leave empty to disable
realIPFromHelp: Only when the original peer (the address in the PROXY header for connections that use the PROXY protocol) is in these ranges is the visitor address read from request headers. It is then used for access logs, IP lists, LAN-only access, country filtering, auth failure bans, statistics and path probing. 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 are not allowed. When Protocol Routing forwards over loopback, have it send a PROXY header instead of adding 127.0.0.1 here.
realIPHeadersPlaceholder: X-Forwarded-For by default; custom header names can be typed
realIPHeadersHelp: Checked in order; the first header that yields a valid address wins. Multi-value headers such as X-Forwarded-For are read right to left, skipping trusted proxies, and the first untrusted address is used. Pick only headers your proxy overwrites.
callbackPlaceholder: https://auth.example.com (must be served by one of Gately's listeners)
callbackHelp: The callback URL to register with GitHub / Google is: {url} (use this same URL for GitHub, Google and QQ)
savedReloaded: Saved. The listener has been reloaded
http3Help: Also serve HTTP/3 (QUIC) on the same port number over UDP. Allow that UDP port in your firewall and port forwarding.
plainHttpHelp: How plain HTTP requests on this port are handled. Redirect sends http://host:port to https://host:port; Serve answers them over unencrypted HTTP.
optSniFromHost: Use the visited domain as SNI
optSniFromHostHelp: HTTPS backends only: send the visitor's domain in the handshake and verify the certificate against it. Needed when the backend routes by SNI (e.g. frp vhost_https); same as nginx proxy_ssl_server_name on
optPassAuthCookiesHelp: Sign-in is handled by the backend Gately: this site has no authentication and passes the single sign-on and session cookies issued by the backend Gately through unchanged. Only enable when the backend is your own Gately
locationTargetsPlaceholder: Backend addresses, comma-separated; leave empty to use the site backends
locationHeadersPlaceholder: Extra request headers, one Key: Value per line
locationsHelp: Send requests under a path prefix to other backends. Longest prefix wins; the path is forwarded unchanged. Same as nginx location /api/ + proxy_pass
redirectHostHelp: Use {'{host}'} for the visitor's domain, e.g. https://{'{host}'} with “Keep path” to send all HTTP to HTTPS
redirectVarsHelp: Also available: {'{path}'}{'{args}'} (original path and query; when used, “Keep path” no longer appends them), {'{port}'}, {'{1}'} (the part matched by * in a site domain like *.example.com), {'{STUN_rule name_PORT}'}, {'{STUN_rule name_IP}'}, {'{STUN_rule name_ADDR}'} (the STUN rule's current public address). E.g. https://{'{1}'}.v4.example.com:{'{STUN_web_PORT}'}{'{path}'}{'{args}'}
cleanUrlsHelp: When a file is missing, also try path.html and path/index.html. For VitePress and similar static sites; same as nginx try_files
forwardAuthUrlHelp: Each request is checked against this URL first and allowed on 2xx, like nginx auth_request. For Authelia use /api/authz/auth-request
forwardAuthLoginHelp: Where to send visitors when the endpoint returns 401. {'{url}'} is the original URL and {'{method}'} the request method. Leave empty to pass the endpoint's response through
sharedUsersDivider: Shared users and OIDC identity provider
sharedUsersHelp: Login accounts shared by several sites, each with optional TOTP two-step verification. A site uses them once “Use shared users” is ticked under web auth; can replace external auth such as Authelia
ssoDomainHelp: e.g. example.com: after a shared user signs in on any site under this domain or its subdomains, the other sites need no further sign-in. Leave empty to sign in per site
selfServicePasswordHelp: When on, shared users can change their own password at {site} on sites with Use shared users enabled, or at {oidc} on the OIDC issuer domain, after entering the current password (and verification code); the login page shows a link too. Afterwards the user's sessions on all sites end immediately, and issued OIDC refresh tokens and Access Tokens are revoked
oidcIntro: Lets Gitea, OpenList, Grafana and other OpenID Connect applications sign users in with the shared users above, so each application knows who is signed in. This can replace Authelia's OIDC provider.
sharedUsersSiteLabel: Use shared users (TOTP and single sign-on)
sharedUsersSiteHelp: Manage shared users on the Auth users page, where you can also select sites in bulk; works alongside the site's own users below
manageUsers: Manage on the Auth users page
manageUsersHelp: Shared users, the single sign-on domain, self-service password change and the OIDC identity provider are managed on the Auth users page, where you can also choose in bulk which sites accept shared users
filterPlaceholder: Search domain, name, group or backend
defaultSiteLast: The default site always comes last
userRouteTargetsPlaceholder: Backends for these users, separated by commas
userRoutesHelp: After sign-in, send each user to a different backend. Users not listed, and visitors who are not signed in on public paths, use the site backends. Use the site user or shared user name, provider-key:id for third-party sign-in, or the Remote-User returned by forward auth. Path rules with their own backends take priority; path rules that only add headers use the user's backends. Like nginx map $remote_user $backend
userHeaderHelp: After sign-in, put the user name in this request header for the backend; the same header sent by visitors is removed. Leave empty to not pass it
emailHeaderHelp: After sign-in, put the user's email in this request header for the backend (for apps that use email as the account, such as Firefly III); the same header sent by visitors is removed. The email comes from the shared user's settings or the Remote-Email returned by forward auth; site users and third-party sign-in pass none. Leave empty to not pass it
probeRuleHelp: Create a Web path probing rule for this listener in Intrusion protection
copySitesHelp: Share links are not copied: their tokens bypass authentication. Create new ones on the copy if needed.
siteGone: The site was not found. It may have been deleted or moved; refresh and try again
siteListenerMoveHelp: The site moves to the chosen listener when saved. Signed-in visitors have to sign in again and statistics start over.
siteMoveConfirm: Save the changes and move the site to "{target}"?
siteMoveFailed: Changes saved, but the move failed: {error}
siteMoved: Saved and moved to the chosen listener
dropHere: Drop here to move into this listener
